title: Weekly price shock alert: Lyocell - week ended July 3
content:
China and Pakistan fell 0.14 per cent while India held flat, leaving lyocell as Asia's one of stable major fibre with all three markets locked within a 0.14-point weekly range.
Lyocell outperformed polyester and viscose as disciplined supply kept prices firm despite softer pulp costs.
Stable pricing strengthens yarn pricing across Asia, while Pakistan's gas-cost shock limits mill profitability.

title: Cambodia, China’s Hainan province vow to expand bilateral trade
content:
China’s Hainan province and Cambodia have reaffirmed their commitment to expand trade and investment cooperation. 
Cambodia’s commerce secretary Lim Lork Piseth met a delegation from the province, and both sides highlighted the strategic importance of the Hainan Free Trade Port as a gateway for deeper economic collaboration. 
Piseth outlined opportunities to expand market access for Cambodian products.

title: Vietnam’s HCM City to cut logistics costs to 11-14% of regional GDP
content:
Vietnam’s HCM City is rolling out a logistics development strategy to reduce costs to 11-14 per cent of its regional GDP by 2030—lower than the national target of 15-16 per cent. 
The aim is to position the city as a modern logistics hub and strengthen its role in global supply chains. 
Ring roads, new expressways, dedicated railway lines and upgraded waterways, are being planned.

title: India’s Jharkhand unveils drafts of industrial, textile policies
content:
India’s Jharkhand state has unveiled the draft versions of the Jharkhand Textile, Apparel & Footwear Policy 2026 and the Jharkhand Industrial Investment Promotion Policy 2026, seeking feedback from stakeholders. 
The latter aims at aligning with key national initiatives, enabling the state to integrate into global value chains and promote high-value segments like tech textiles and MMF products.

title: Levi's Q2 to test apparel's new tariff-driven margin playbook
content:
Levi's Q2 could become the apparel industry's first real benchmark for post-IEEPA tariff economics. 
With just ~1 per cent China sourcing, a potential $35 million COGS benefit, $0.07 EPS upside and an $80 million tariff refund in play, its guidance will determine whether diversified sourcing now delivers a structural margin edge—and reshape sourcing, pricing and supplier strategies across global apparel.

title: ICE cotton advances on US weather concerns, grain market rally
content:
ICE cotton futures rose over 1.5 per cent, supported by US weather concerns and a rally in CBOT grain markets, marking the fourth gain in five sessions.
Limited rainfall in US cotton areas and delayed crop development in India underpinned sentiment, while USDA lowered the US cotton crop's good-to-excellent rating.
Trading volumes remained light despite the price rally.

title: Bangladesh invites US firms to expand investment
content:
Bangladesh has invited US firms to expand their investments in the country, assuring policy stability, equal treatment and a more business-friendly environment.
PM's adviser Mahdi Amin made this request while addressing a programme marking the 250th anniversary of US independence. 
He identified energy, textiles and high-value manufacturing as sectors with strong potential for expanded cooperation.

title: New Zealand sees stronger India demand ahead of FTA rollout
content:
New Zealand exporters report stronger India demand before the FTA, with engagement extending to wool, forestry, chip, and pulp. 
Indian wool delegations sought premium fibres, processing technology, and advisory expertise, signalling textile sourcing interest. 
The FTA is before Parliament and expected later in 2026; 57 per cent of New Zealand exports to India will be tariff-free from day one.

title: Bangladesh RMG exports down 1.6% to $38.7 bn in FY26; June rebounds
content:
Bangladesh's RMG exports fell 1.64 per cent to $38.70 billion in FY  2025-26, with knitwear declining more than woven apparel.
However, June exports rebounded strongly, rising 21.52 per cent year on year.
Home textile exports grew during both the fiscal year and June, while cotton product exports declined for the full year despite June gains.
